claims.statement: The repository is a single multi-module Maven reactor: root pom.xml declares parent cn.shopex:ecshopx with version ${revision}=5.5.0 (Java 17) under spring-boot-starter-parent:3.5.12, with 53 modules total — four infrastructure modules (ecshopx-bom, ecshopx-common, ecshopx-dispatch, ecshopx-bootstrap) and 49 business Bundles including ecshopx-digios, ecshopx-openapi, and ecshopx-shuyun — each also pinned in dependencyManagement, and ecshopx-bootstrap's POM declares all 49 business Bundles.
ecshopx-bom is a pom-packaging bill-of-materials module that imports spring-boot-dependencies:3.5.12 and pins MyBatis-Plus 3.5.16 and Lombok 1.18.36 versions.

ecshopx-bootstrap is the only Spring Boot executable: it declares all 49 business Bundles plus runtime starters (Undertow replacing Tomcat, Data Redis, AMQP, Flyway core+mysql, MySQL connector, xxl-job-core 2.5.0), and re-enables spring-boot-maven-plugin with skip=false and mainClass=cn.shopex.ecshopx.EcshopxApplication while the parent POM sets skip=true for all other modules.

EcshopxApplication is the single entry annotated with @SpringBootApplication(scanBasePackages="cn.shopex.ecshopx") and @MapperScan(basePackages="cn.shopex.ecshopx.**.mapper") using FqcnMapperBeanNameGenerator with lazyInitialization=true: the FQCN-based bean names avoid same-name Mapper collisions across ~48 Bundles, placing @MapperScan on the main class registers MapperFactoryBean during primary-config processing so MyBatis-Plus auto-scanning backs off, and lazy init bounds the large context's startup cost.

The app listens on server.port=18080 via embedded Undertow (bootstrap excludes spring-boot-starter-tomcat and adds spring-boot-starter-undertow), with allow-unescaped-characters-in-url=true and max-http-post-size=64MB configured for PHP-era URL/upload compatibility.

UndertowMultipartMaxEntityCustomizer raises Undertow's separate multipart entity cap (default near 2MB) to 64MB so Spring's multipart limits (50MB file / 55MB request) govern uploads, and enables ALLOW_ENCODED_SLASH so encoded %2F reaches the servlet mapping layer.

Three externally meaningful URL spaces exist: /api/… (business controllers under api/admin/v1 and api/front/v1, admin under /api/v1, buyer H5/Mini Program under /api/v1/h5app, plus the /api/openapi gateway from ecshopx-openapi), /storage/** (StorageWebMvcConfigurer in ecshopx-espier, active only when ecshopx.storage.driver=local, maps ecshopx.storage.local.root to a static resource handler), and /wechatAuth/… (unauthenticated callback controllers such as WxpayNotifyController at /wechatAuth/wxpay/notify, WechatOpenPlatformMessageCallbackController at /wechatAuth/callback/{authorizerAppId}, WxappLegacyQrcodeController at /wechatAuth/wxapp/qrcode.png).

StrictHttpFirewallConfig installs a StorageAwareHttpFirewall that applies Spring Security's StrictHttpFirewall (with encoded-slash, double-slash, semicolon relaxations) to every path except /storage/**, which uses the lenient DefaultHttpFirewall so local-disk image URLs with Chinese/mojibake filenames pass; StorageUnicodeHttpFirewallTest pins both sides.

Flyway runs at startup (spring.flyway.enabled=true, locations=classpath:db/migration, baseline-on-migrate=true, baseline-version=0) with migrations only in ecshopx-bootstrap/src/main/resources/db/migration (V00000000000001.sql, V00000000000002.sql); existing databases imported from docker/ecshopx.sql are baselined at version 0 instead of replaying history, and bin/make-migration generates VyyyyMMddHHmmss__description.sql files by diffing the live schema against MyBatis-Plus annotations.

After Flyway, MigrationSeedRunner (ApplicationRunner in bootstrap) aligns seed data with the PHP EspierBundle UpdateMenuListener: it imports logistics companies only when the logistics table is empty (failure logs but does not block startup), and when common.use-system-menu=true it atomically deletes all company_id=0 system menus and their menu-type relations, then re-imports six role-based JSON seed files under classpath:seed/menu/ (platform, it, shop, dealer, merchant, supplier) in fixed order via ShopMenuUploadService.uploadMenus, inside a programmatic TransactionTemplate transaction so a proxied @Transactional cannot be bypassed by the self-call.

MultiRedisConfig bypasses Spring Boot Redis auto-configuration and builds custom Lettuce factories (TCP keepalive, autoReconnect, validateConnection, configurable command/connect timeouts via ecshopx.redis.lettuce.*) for named logical databases: springDataRedisConnectionFactory/sharedStringRedisTemplate/dispatchBusStringRedisTemplate (spring.data.redis.database, default 0), companys (ecshopx.redis.companys.database, default 0, @Primary template), prism (default 2), datacube (default 0), deposit (default 1), members/espier/wechat (each falling back to spring.data.redis.database); deposit/members/espier/wechat factories also accept dedicated ecshopx.redis.<name>.host|port|password overrides.

XXL-JOB 2.5.0 handles all scheduled work: XxlJobConfig in bootstrap creates an XxlJobSpringExecutor (appname ecshopx-executor, executor port 19999, admin addresses defaulting to http://127.0.0.1:9080/xxl-job-admin in application.properties but overridden to http://xxl-job-admin:8080/xxl-job-admin by both Docker Compose stacks, accessToken ecshopx-cron-dev, 7-day log retention); the admin console is a separate xuxueli/xxl-job-admin:2.5.0 container with its xxl_job schema in the same MySQL.

Business cron handlers are @XxlJob("<short-name>") methods in each Bundle's cron/ package (e.g. orders/cron/ScheduleFinishOrdersHandler under name finish-orders); the uniform shape invokes the cron service, logs cost, and on exception publishes a CronAlertEvent Spring ApplicationEvent from common/cron/event for alerting, then rethrows so XXL-JOB records the failure.

The dispatch bus is wired by bootstrap's DispatchBusConfig: DispatchFacade → DispatchCore.asyncReady with an InMemoryDispatchRegistry, SyncDispatchDriver, and only the Redis driver mapped (DispatchDriverType has SYNC/REDIS/RABBITMQ but RabbitMQ classes are not registered in the default configuration); RedisDispatchDriver is bound to dispatchBusStringRedisTemplate with dispatch: queue prefix and dispatch:delayed ZSET for delayed messages moved by RedisDelayedDispatchMover; DispatchConsumerRuntime, DispatchRetryDecider, FailedJobRecorder, and DispatchStructuredLogger complete the pipeline.

RedisDispatchListener polls (default every 1s via dispatch.redis.poll-delay-ms) popping one message from dispatch:default then up to dispatch.redis.slow.batch-size (default 20) each from dispatch:slow and dispatch:sms, feeding each decoded payload to DispatchConsumerRuntime — queue names act as load-class signals (exports/statistics/finish-order jobs go to slow, SMS work to sms, everything else to default).

Bootstrap installs a stub FailedJobMapper bean that returns 1 instead of a MyBatis-Plus-backed implementation — persistence of dispatch failed_jobs is a wiring point to be completed rather than production-grade today.

AsyncExecutorConfig (@EnableAsync) defines 15 named ThreadPoolTaskExecutor beans for per-concern @Async work (omeFromOmeSyncExecutor, employeePurchaseExportExecutor, jushuitanUploadExecutor, vipGradeBatchExecutor, communityOrderExportExecutor, ordersFinancialSalesreportExportExecutor, ordersRightsExportExecutor, ordersOrderExportDataExecutor, salespersonSubtaskSlowExecutor, promotionsGiveSlowExecutor, espierUploadFileSlowExecutor, aftersalesShopApplyExecutor, aftersalesFinancialExportSlowExecutor, dispatchBusInternalExecutor, shuyunOfflineBenefitSendExecutor).

Three deployment paths share the same topology: full development (dev-setup.sh / install.sh --full → docker-compose.dev.yml with mysql:8.0 importing docker/tables_xxl_job.sql then docker/ecshopx.sql, redis:7-alpine with password redispassword and AOF, xxl-job-admin:2.5.0, and ecshopx-app built from docker/Dockerfile.app exposing ports 80/18080/19999 with APP_ARGS CLI-style property injection), lite offline (docker-lite/deploy.sh / install.sh --lite → docker-lite/docker-compose.yml with a prebuilt image bind-mounting the jar), and self-hosted jar runs. For the self-hosted jar, local overrides come from environment variables, CLI-style arguments (e.g. --spring.datasource.url=…, --spring.config.additional-location=file:./config/), or an external config location: ecshopx-bootstrap/src/main/resources/application-local.properties is git-ignored (.gitignore line 7) and absent from fresh checkouts, so the readme's claim that the project "already includes" it is drift.

Inside the ecshopx-app container, an OpenResty/nginx front on port 80 (docker/app-nginx.conf) routes by Host (ADMIN_HOST/H5_HOST/PC_HOST): /api/, /storage/, and /wechatAuth/ are proxied to the Java process at 127.0.0.1:18080 while static frontends are served from /data/httpd, keeping URL spaces identical to the PHP deployment.

Each of the 48 business Bundles declares its domain in a Chinese package-info.java at its package root; the catalog spans core commerce (goods 商品域, orders 订单/购物车/物流/结算域, aftersales 售后域, members 会员与账户域, comments 评论域, deposit 储值域, supplier 供应商域, cross-border 跨境电商域), marketing (promotions, kaquan, point, pointsmall, distribution, popularize, employee-purchase, community, wsugc, form, reservation, one-code, shopex-ai), stores/operations (merchant, companys, salesperson, selfservice, super-admin, shopmenu-border, im), payments (payment, adapay, hfpay, bspay, chinaums-pay), WeChat (wechat, work-wechat), and integrations/platform (ali, aliyunsms, shuyun, system-link, youshu, kujiale, tb-items, third-party, openapi, espier, theme, tdkset, data-cube).

ecshopx-bootstrap's config/ package is where cross-Bundle edges are wired: ~160 *DispatchPublisherImpl components implement ecshopx-common publisher interfaces by calling DispatchFacade with the correct mode/driver/queue/delay/retry tuple, and ~200 *RegistrationConfig classes call dispatchRegistry.registerJob/registerEventListener in @PostConstruct — the explicit wiring that keeps producer and consumer Bundles Maven-decoupled.

ecshopx-common contains ~150 files under common/dispatch (publisher port interfaces like FinishOrderJobDispatchPublisher plus per-Bundle *DispatchJobNames / *DispatchEventNames constants) that keep cross-Bundle wiring acyclic: producing Bundles depend only on the interface, and bootstrap supplies the implementation that publishes onto the bus with legacy-PHP-preserving message names.

The business Bundle inventory at HEAD includes ecshopx-digios, a DigiOS POS direct-integration module declared in the root pom.xml modules list, pinned in dependencyManagement, and assembled by ecshopx-bootstrap; unlike the other Bundles it carries no package-info.java domain declaration (its domain is stated only in its POM description).

The current Flyway schema head is V00000000000006.sql (release 5.4.7): it creates members_rel_tags_audit (attach/detach audit trail with source, rule_version, reason, event_id, indexed on company_id,user_id,tag_id), adds source/rule_version/effective_at/updated_at to members_rel_tags, adds tag_code/tag_kind (manual|system)/rule_version plus a uk_company_tag_code unique key to members_tags, and adds member_tag_ids (JSON)/member_tag_mode (include|exclude) to both promotions_marketing_activity and promotions_seckill_activity.

POS terminal authentication is exposed at /api/v1/pos/auth by PosAuthController (ecshopx-companys api/pos/v1) with POST /login (employee number + password → POS JWT), POST /logout (blacklists the presented token), and GET /me (role/permission snapshot read from the POS_JWT_USER_DATA request attribute installed by the filter).

PosAuthService (companys service/posauth) authenticates POS logins by looking up the pos_store_account row by employee number, decrypting the stored password cipher through SensitiveFieldEncryptor, rejecting disabled/resigned accounts and accounts whose shop no longer allows login, then delegates token issuance to the PosJwtIssuerPort interface defined in ecshopx-common/auth — keeping ecshopx-companys decoupled from the espier JWT implementation.

PosJwtIssuer (ecshopx-espier/security, implementing common's PosJwtIssuerPort) signs HS512 compact POS JWTs keyed from JWT_SECRET with claims token_kind=pos, issuer POS_JWT_ISSUER (default ecshopx-pos), a random jti, and TTL from JWT_TTL minutes; invalidate() (logout) verifies the token and blacklists it via PosJwtBlacklistService, which stores pos_jwt_invalidate:<sha256(token)> keys with exp-derived TTL on the prism Redis template (logical DB 2 by default).

PosJwtAuthenticationFilter (ecshopx-espier/security, OncePerRequestFilter at HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE+40) engages only when the Bearer token parses as a POS token (token_kind=pos or the POS issuer, skipping POST /api/v1/pos/auth/login and all non-POS requests), then enforces PosJwtPathWhitelist (auth endpoints, order/aftersales/checkout prefixes, operator cart paths, goods/member/tag/logistics reads, delivery and write-off POSTs, explicit deny on /api/v1/store/pos-accounts), rejects blacklisted or expired tokens, and calls PosJwtSessionValidatorPort before attaching the claims map as the POS_JWT_USER_DATA request attribute.

PosJwtSessionValidator (companys service/posauth, implementing common's PosJwtSessionValidatorPort) re-reads the pos_store_account row on every POS request and invalidates the token immediately when the account is disabled, resigned, reassigned to another store, or re-roled (spec rule G-L9), so status/distributor_id/role changes take effect without waiting for JWT expiry.

POS store account provisioning reaches the dispatch bus through common's PosStoreAccountCreateEventDispatchPublisher port: bootstrap's PosStoreAccountCreateEventDispatchPublisherImpl publishes event:companys:pos_store_account_create (CompanysDispatchEventNames.EVENT_POS_STORE_ACCOUNT_CREATE) so DigiOS account-sync listeners can consume it without a companys→digios Maven edge.

Bootstrap's config package registers the ecshopx-digios sync listeners through five DigiOs*DispatchListenerRegistrationConfig classes (operator create, distributor create/update, and normal-order-delivery/aftersales-return store adjustments), each wiring a digios listener to its event name from ecshopx-common with async ListenerDispatchOptions on the default queue.

Each seed menu file (e.g. platform_menu.json) is a JSON array of rows whose version groups a menu generation, menu_type names the menu types the row belongs to, and name_lang carries per-locale names (zh-CN, en-CN, ar-SA, zh-TW, ja-JP, ru-RU); ShopMenuUploadService.uploadMenus (@Transactional per file) first deletes existing company_id=0 rows of the incoming versions including their shop_menu_rel_type rows and name_lang translations written through companys' CommonLangModWriteService, then re-inserts rows with fresh sequential shopmenu_ids, remaps file-local pid values to the new parent ids, rebuilds menu-type relations, re-writes translations, and rejects rows missing alias_name.

The current Flyway schema head is V00000000000007.sql (release 5.5.0): it adds merchant-settlement onboarding fields (contact_name, main_category_selection JSON, license_registered_address, license_legal_representative) to merchant, adds those plus user_id to merchant_settlement_apply, and adds a uk_company_user (company_id, user_id) unique key so each member can file at most one settlement application per company.

ecshopx-openapi guards the /api/openapi/** public gateway: OpenapiWebMvcConfigurer registers OpenapiAuthInterceptor on the public and internal path patterns; the interceptor skips /api/openapi/internal paths, requires version/timestamp/app_key, enforces a ±600 s timestamp tolerance, verifies the sign via OpenapiSignSupport against OpenapiDeveloperLookupPort credentials, and then calls OpenapiSignedRequestReplayGuard.assertOnce, which SETNXs openapi:auth:replay:{sha256(app_key|sign|timestamp)} on the default StringRedisTemplate with a 600 s TTL — a replayed app_key+sign+timestamp within the window is rejected; openapi.debug=1 bypasses signature and replay checks as the system company.

ecshopx-digios (DigiOS POS direct integration, declared in its POM description rather than a package-info.java) is bidirectional on the dispatch bus: it consumes companys/distribution events via the bootstrap DigiOs*DispatchListenerRegistrationConfig wiring and also publishes its own store adjustments — DigiOsAftersalesReturnAdjustmentDispatchPublisherImpl plus the DigiOsAftersalesReturnAdjustment and DigiOsNormalOrderDeliveryAdjustment listener registrations let DigiOS originate aftersales-return and order-delivery stock adjustments.

ecshopx-shuyun is the Shuyun (数云) CRM integration Bundle covering the legacy UAPI and the open-platform open-api; bootstrap subscribes 12 ShuyunOpenPlatform*DispatchListenerRegistrationConfig listeners (member create, distributor create/update, order pay/delivery/confirm/cancel, refund finish, offline benefit consume, item-store product sync) to their bus events.

OpenapiSignedRequestReplayGuardTest and OpenapiAuthInterceptorReplayTest pin the OpenAPI replay-guard semantics: the first sighting of an app_key+sign+timestamp passes and an identical replay within the TTL window is rejected.
